# Issues and labels

All paths begin `/api/v1`. Session mutations send `X-Crew-Request: 1`; API tokens require the named scope in addition to the actor's project access. Members write issues; guests read only granted projects. Lists accept `limit` (1–200, default 50), opaque `cursor`, and return `{items,nextCursor}`. Organization issue lists apply project access before pagination.

`GET/POST /projects/:projectId/issues` lists or creates issues. `GET /orgs/:orgId/issues` lists accessible organization issues. Filters are `statusId`, `assigneeId`, `labelId`, `priority`, `q` (case insensitive key/title/description substring). `GET/PATCH/DELETE /issues/:issueId` reads, updates or deletes an issue. Read needs `project:read`; mutation needs `issue:write`. Archived projects remain readable and reject mutations with 409.

Create takes `{title,description,statusId,priority,assigneeId,estimate,dueDate,parentId,labelIds}`. Title is 1–300 characters. Description preserves Markdown whitespace and is at most 100000 characters. Omitted status uses the first ordered workflow state. Priority is 0 none, 1 urgent, 2 high, 3 normal, 4 low. Estimate is nullable, finite, between 0 and 1000000; fractions and zero are valid. Due date is nullable YYYY-MM-DD and must be a real calendar date. Assignee needs project access. Parent must be in the same project and cannot create a cycle. Every label must belong to the project. PATCH retains omitted fields and accepts null for assignee, estimate, due date and parent; `labelIds:[]` clears labels. Unknown fields and invalid inputs return 422 with field details.

Issue keys use the project key and sequential number. Numbers allocate transactionally; failed requests do not consume them and deletion does not reuse them. Public issues include all fields plus `id,orgId,projectId,projectKey,number,key,statusName,statusCategory,assignee,creator,createdBy,rank,labels,createdAt,updatedAt`. No password or token fields are exposed.

`GET/POST /projects/:projectId/labels` lists or creates `{name,color}`. Names are unique within a project ignoring case; colors use six hexadecimal digits such as `#5965d8`. `PATCH/DELETE /labels/:labelId` updates or removes a label. Removing one also removes assignments. Label changes emit updated full issue snapshots for affected issues so indexes stay current.

The web offers project issue filters with cursor loading, complete create/edit forms, parent and label controls, issue detail and child links, and a label manager. Required and invalid fields have accessible errors. Destructive operations ask for confirmation.

CLI: `crew issue list PROJECT [--status ID --assignee ID --label ID --priority N --query TEXT --limit N --cursor CURSOR]`, `create PROJECT --title TEXT`, `show ISSUE`, `edit ISSUE`, `delete ISSUE --yes`. Create/edit support `--description`, `--description-file`, `--status`, `--priority`, `--assignee`, `--estimate`, `--due`, `--parent`, `--labels ID,ID`. Use `none` to clear nullable fields or labels. Label actions are `labels PROJECT`, `label-create PROJECT --name TEXT [--color HEX]`, `label-edit LABEL`, `label-delete LABEL --yes`. All commands support global `--json`, `--url`, `--token`, `--config`.

## Integration schema and events

Migrations 200–249 belong to W1. `issues(id,project_id,number,title,description,status_id,priority,assignee_id,estimate,due_date,parent_id,created_by,rank,created_at,updated_at)` stores issue content. `labels(id,project_id,name,color,created_at,updated_at)` and `issue_labels(issue_id,label_id)` store project label assignments. Parent deletion clears children; issue deletion cascades assignments. Project deletion cascades issues and labels.

`modules/work/issues.js` exports the canonical `getIssue(ctx,id)` hydrated reader, `publicIssue(row)`, `listIssues(ctx,projectId,query)`, `createIssue`, `updateIssue`, `deleteIssue`, `emitIssue`, `validateIssueReferences` and `replaceIssueLabels`. Consumers should reuse `getIssue` rather than create another encoder. `publicIssue` takes the joined issueSelect row; use getIssue for labels.

Issue events use entityType `issue`, action `created`, `updated`, `deleted`, full before/after snapshots, actorId, orgId, projectId, entityId and UTC time. Label events use entityType `label` and the same actions. Emit occurs after the synchronous transaction has committed. Full issue after data contains descriptions, assignee identity, creator identity and label objects for search and notification consumers.

## Comments, Markdown and mentions

GET/POST /issues/:issueId/comments lists or creates {body}. PATCH/DELETE /comments/:commentId edits or removes a comment. Reads need project:read; writes need comment:write. An author can edit/remove their own comments; an organization owner/admin may manage other comments. Granted guests can comment. Archived projects reject discussion writes. Lists are chronological and cursor paginated. Comments return author identity, original body, safe html, mentionedUserIds and timestamps.

Markdown supports headings, paragraphs, line breaks, ordered/unordered/task lists, block quotes, horizontal rules, inline/fenced code, emphasis, bold, strikeout and links. All raw HTML and attribute delimiters are escaped. Only http, https and mailto links are active. Code never produces mentions. Mention syntax is @handle, @email, @{userId}, or @[Display name](user:userId). Name/email/id matching is case insensitive and resolves only organization members with access to this project. The web mention picker inserts explicit IDs to avoid name ambiguity. Unknown mentions remain text. No HTML is trusted from the user.

Comment events use entityType comment and created/updated/deleted actions. After contains the full comment, a hydrated issue snapshot, mentionedUserIds and userIds; event also has issueId and mentionedUserIds. Consumers can subscribe creator, assignee and mentioned users through these IDs. Table comments(id,issue_id,author_id,body,created_at,updated_at) cascades on issue deletion. Reuse getComment(ctx,id), listComments(ctx,issueId), publicComment(ctx,row).

## Issue relations

GET/POST /issues/:issueId/relations lists or creates {targetIssueId,kind}. DELETE /relations/:relationId removes a relation. Reads need project:read and hide inaccessible opposite endpoints before pagination. Writes need issue:write on both projects and both must be in the same organization and unarchived. Self relations are invalid. blocks and duplicates are directed source to target; their inverse views read blocked by and duplicated by. An issue can duplicate only one original. Directed cycles are rejected. relates is symmetric, stored in canonical ID order; reversed duplicates return 409. Different relation kinds may coexist.

Relations return sourceIssueId,targetIssueId,kind,direction,caption,relatedIssue,createdBy,createdAt. Table issue_relations(id,source_issue_id,target_issue_id,kind,created_by,created_at) cascades when either issue is deleted. Events use entityType relation and created/deleted actions with complete before/after relation, issueId, actor/org/project identity and UTC time.

CLI discussion actions: comments ISSUE, comment ISSUE --body TEXT (or --body-file FILE), comment-edit COMMENT --body TEXT, comment-delete COMMENT --yes, relations ISSUE, relate ISSUE --target ISSUE --kind blocks|duplicates|relates, unrelate RELATION --yes. The issue page offers Markdown previews, mention picker, comment editing/removal and relation controls with inverse labels.

## Issue editor candidates

GET /projects/:projectId/assignees requires project:read and returns cursor-paginated {userId,name,email,role,createdAt} records for organization members who can read that project. Project visibility is applied before pagination. Both assignee and mention pickers use this endpoint; unrelated organization guests do not appear. All issue forms now use searchable bounded picker pages with independent selected-value resolution, including existing values outside the current page. Detail reads the existing parent directly, and child lists query their own paged resource. The server remains authoritative for access, project membership and ancestry validation.

## Complete work reference controls

`GET /projects/:projectId/issue-options` takes `type=users|labels|parents|relations`, `permission=project:read|issue:write|comment:write` (default project:read), optional `issueId`, `q`, selected `id`, `limit` and `cursor`. It returns `{items,nextCursor,total}` with choices `{id,label,description,...}`. Current role, project access and requested token scope are checked before matching, counts and pagination; this endpoint requires no insight scope. The web reuses EntityPicker through a work API adapter; the insight options implementation is unchanged.

Users are organization members with access to this project, including explicitly granted guests. Labels belong to this project. Parent choices belong to this project and exclude the edited issue and its complete transitive descendant set before paging. A supplied source issue must belong to this project. Relation choices require issue:write on the source and every target, span live projects in the same organization, and exclude self. The relation mutation still validates kind, cycles, duplicate edges, scope and archive state at save time. An independently resolved selected ID still passes all eligibility checks and does not reveal inaccessible records.

Issue list GET also accepts `parentId` for direct child lists. Label list GET accepts case-insensitive `q`; the existing assignee list accepts `q` and selected `id` after access filtering. `GET /labels/:labelId` and `GET /comments/:commentId` return authorized individual snapshots. These use project:read and disclose no unauthorized record.

The issue list, child list, discussion, relation list and label manager show bounded 20-row pages and explicit Load more / Reload controls. Filters and route changes replace list ownership synchronously; late earlier responses cannot append records, errors or cursors into the new resource. Repeated clicks on a pending cursor submit one request. Forms and label/comment edit state belong to their project or issue; they cannot carry into another resource. Loading, empty, permission, archive and field-error states remain visible. Relation rows show readable project keys and inverse captions, and removal remains an explicitly confirmed action.

## Safe editing and draft custody

Issues, labels and comments expose an opaque `revision` calculated from their complete current snapshot. PATCH accepts an optional `expectedRevision`. When present, a stale snapshot returns 409 CONFLICT with `details.expectedRevision` and the authorized `details.current` snapshot before any data changes or mutation event. Invalid revision syntax returns 422. Existing clients may omit the precondition; clients that must prevent lost updates should always send it. A repeated timestamp cannot hide a changed snapshot.

Web issue, comment and label editors send their baseline revision and retain the local draft on validation, conflict and access failures. Inspect latest version performs a new authorized read. Load latest version explicitly confirms replacement of the local draft. Issue and comment editors also offer Keep my changes on latest version, a deliberate reconciliation followed by a separate Save. The issue editor sends only fields changed from its baseline, preserving concurrent untouched fields during reconciliation, including explicit null clearing and label replacement. Permission loss or deletion disables Save while preserving the draft for copying or cancellation. Cancel discards that form explicitly; route navigation starts a form for the new resource.

Descriptions and comments provide escaped Markdown previews and searchable authorized mention pickers from every candidate page. Mention selection inserts an explicit user reference, preserving identity when names collide. Selected labels remain visible independently of search and pagination and have explicit remove controls; clearing an assignee or parent sends null.

CLI additions: `crew issue options PROJECT --type users|labels|parents|relations [--permission PERMISSION] [--issue SOURCE] [--query TEXT] [--selected ID] [--limit N] [--cursor CURSOR]`, `children ISSUE [--limit N --cursor CURSOR]`, `comment-show COMMENT`, and `label-show LABEL`. Issue/comment/label edit accepts `--if-revision REVISION` from the corresponding show response, rejecting a stale update without overwriting the saved resource. `issue labels PROJECT --query TEXT` filters before pagination. Commands print nextCursor for deliberate navigation.

Verification is maintained in server/test/issue-depth.test.js (later-than-200 candidates, whole ancestry, authorization, cross-project references, revision/event guards), web/test/issue-paging.test.js (request generations and adapter protocol), web/test/issue-browser.test.js with pinned Selenium (real fields, Markdown, mentions, relations, labels, revision/access drafts and delayed navigation), and cli/test/issues.test.js (actual CLI/server reference and precondition flows). These checks are functional diagnostics with unknown OS cache, not performance measurements.

Deletion activity uses the canonical parsed-after / parsed-before snapshot fallback in both relation visibility and issue-scoped filtering. Stored JSON null in a deletion after snapshot cannot mask the before snapshot or turn a successful mutation into a notification error. Visibility still checks both currently accessible relation endpoints before filters, counts or cursors. Watched deletion and grant-revocation regressions retain this integration contract.
Symmetric and directed relation activity belongs to both endpoint issue feeds, independent of canonical storage orientation; each feed applies the same current authorization for both projects.

## Exact supported Markdown subset

Crew uses one canonical parser for rendering and mention extraction in descriptions, comments, previews and notification inputs. Code never creates a semantic mention. Supported blocks are ATX headings level 1–6, paragraphs with line breaks, horizontal rules, ordered/unordered/task lists, blockquotes, fenced and indented code. Lists and quotes can nest, with item continuation lines measured relative to the list marker's content indentation. Ordinary unindented paragraph continuations stay in the current list item or quote; blank lines or a new block end that lazy continuation. Nested code must retain its enclosing list indentation or quote marker. A quote fence ends at its quote container boundary. Tabs in leading indentation expand at four-column stops. Four-space indented code begins a block, but indentation alone cannot interrupt an existing paragraph.

Code spans use matching exact-length backtick runs, allowing different-length runs inside. Span newlines become spaces; one surrounding space pair is trimmed when the content is not all spaces. Fences use at least three backticks or tildes, open with at most three spaces of indentation after container prefixes, and close with the same character repeated at least as many times and no trailing text. An unclosed fence consumes its remaining container. Info text is accepted; only a safe initial language word becomes a CSS class. Backtick info cannot contain a backtick. Backslash escapes suppress delimiters outside code; backslashes inside code stay literal.

Inline formatting includes balanced single/double/triple emphasis markers, strikeout, escaped punctuation, code, readable explicit mentions and links. Links support balanced brackets in labels and parentheses in destinations, escaped delimiters and inline formatting/code in the label; only validated http, https and mailto destinations produce anchors. Unsafe or malformed complete link forms remain escaped text. Raw HTML always remains escaped. Images, tables, HTML blocks, link titles, reference links and automatic URL linking are outside this subset. Nesting is parsed through 32 container/inline levels; deeper content is rendered literally and cannot manufacture semantic mentions. This is a documented safe subset, not a claim of full CommonMark compatibility.

Canonical tests in shared/test/markdown-depth.test.js cover code delimiter lengths, fences, escapes, indentation, nested containers, safe balanced links and malformed inputs. server/test/markdown-work.test.js verifies actual issue/comment mention arrays and absence of code-triggered notifications with a positive outside-code notification control. The pinned work browser Markdown mode checks the same code/mention separation in both description and comment previews.

## Shared Markdown editing commands

Descriptions and comments use the same accessible editing widget and the canonical parser for previews. Its toolbar inserts headings, bold, italic, strikeout, quotes, bullet/numbered/task lists, inline code, fenced code and validated links. Commands work on the current textarea selection and restore focus, caret range and forward/backward selection. Toolbar arrow keys, Home and End move between commands. Write source and Preview preserve the textarea and selection while switching the visible panel. Draft values and resource/revision ownership remain in the parent issue/comment form.

Ctrl or Command+B applies bold, I italic, E inline code and K opens the link field. Ctrl or Command+Alt+1–6 selects a heading level; Shift+X applies strikeout, Shift+7 a numbered list and Shift+8 a bullet list. Composition events and unrelated shortcuts retain normal behavior. Inline placeholders stay selected for immediate replacement. Line commands operate on complete selected lines, normalize compatible prefixes and keep the original content selected; reapplying the same block kind removes that prefix.

Code insertion chooses a backtick run longer than every run in the selected content, with at least three for fences. Inline padding keeps boundary backticks and meaningful spaces from merging into delimiters. Fences add required line boundaries and retain the selected content, including existing fences, literally. Links accept only the same safe http/https/mailto policy as rendering, escape label/destination delimiters and preserve the draft/selection on invalid URLs. Formatting that exceeds a field's existing maximum length reports an error without replacing its value. The original description/body textarea names remain stable.

web/test/markdown-commands.test.js verifies selection serialization, Unicode offsets, toggles, safe code and link output, line boundaries and shortcuts. The actual pinned work browser toolbar mode exercises keyboard bold, safe code fencing and preview/source selection restoration in descriptions, toolbar keyboard navigation, invalid URL custody, valid link insertion, heading shortcuts and safe comment preview.

## Lazy project issue hierarchy

The project issues page offers List view and Hierarchy view. The same authorized issue list accepts `parentId=null` for roots (an issue with no parent) or an issue ID for direct children. The status, assignee, label, priority and search filters select roots only in Hierarchy view. Expanding a matching root loads all its direct children without those filters, preserving ancestry context; each deeper expansion follows the same rule. List view retains its normal whole-project matching.

Each tree branch, including roots, has an independent 20-row cursor, pending request, loading, empty and error state. Load more has no total item cap. Collapse releases descendant page ownership; responses from that collapsed generation cannot reappear after expansion. Filter/project/view changes dispose the previous tree, and delayed responses cannot enter the replacement. A current 401/403/404 hides that branch's retained rows and exposes explicit reload. Reads use project:read and need no insight scope; guest grants are checked by the same canonical endpoint.

The tree exposes tree/treeitem/group semantics, a roving item focus and readable issue links. Up/Down traverse visible issues, Right expands then enters the first child, Left collapses or returns to the parent, Home/End select the first/last visible issue, and Enter opens its issue link. Visible expand/collapse, links, reload and load-more controls remain directly usable. Async expansion enters its first child only while that request still owns the branch; Load more focuses its first newly added issue. Collapsing a focused descendant restores its ancestor, and replacement resources select their first visible item.

Pure hierarchy, canonical HTTP and pinned Chromium proofs live in the dedicated issue-hierarchy test files. These remain functional diagnostics with unknown cache state.

import json, signal, sys
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.webdriver.common.keys import Keys
from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC
s=json.loads(sys.argv[1]); driver=None
signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM,lambda *args: (_ for _ in ()).throw(TimeoutError('Hierarchy deadline'))); signal.alarm(50)
try:
    options=webdriver.ChromeOptions(); options.binary_location='/usr/bin/chromium'
    for flag in ['--headless=new','--no-sandbox','--disable-dev-shm-usage','--window-size=1440,1200']: options.add_argument(flag)
    driver=webdriver.Chrome(service=Service('/usr/bin/chromedriver'),options=options);driver.set_page_load_timeout(8);wait=WebDriverWait(driver,6)
    driver.get(s['url']);name,value=s['cookie'].split('=',1);driver.add_cookie({'name':name,'value':value,'path':'/'})
    driver.execute_cdp_cmd('Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument',{'source':"window.originalFetch=fetch.bind(window);window.fetch=(url,options)=>{const result=window.originalFetch(url,options);return window.hold&&String(url).includes(window.hold)&&String(url).includes('cursor=')?result.then(r=>new Promise(resolve=>window.release=()=>resolve(r))):result}"})
    driver.get(s['url']+'/?tree-proof=1#/projects/'+s['projectId']+'/issues')
    def button(text):return wait.until(EC.element_to_be_clickable((By.XPATH,'//button[normalize-space()="'+text+'"]')))
    def item(id):return wait.until(EC.presence_of_element_located((By.CSS_SELECTOR,'[role="treeitem"][data-issue-id="'+id+'"]')))
    def focused(id):wait.until(lambda d:d.execute_script('return document.activeElement.dataset.issueId')==id)
    button('Hierarchy view').click();wait.until(lambda d:len(d.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'[role="tree"] > [role="treeitem"]'))==20)
    button('Load more root issues').click();wait.until(lambda d:len(d.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'[role="tree"] > [role="treeitem"]'))==25)
    q=driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'input[name="q"]');q.send_keys('Explore root');wait.until(lambda d:len(d.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'[role="treeitem"]'))==1)
    root=item(s['rootId']);root.send_keys(Keys.ARROW_RIGHT);focused(s['firstChildId']);item(s['firstChildId']).send_keys(Keys.ARROW_RIGHT);focused(s['deepId'])
    assert item(s['deepId']).get_attribute('aria-level')=='3'
    item(s['deepId']).send_keys(Keys.ARROW_LEFT);focused(s['firstChildId']);item(s['firstChildId']).send_keys(Keys.ARROW_LEFT);assert item(s['firstChildId']).get_attribute('aria-expanded')=='false'
    item(s['firstChildId']).send_keys(Keys.HOME);focused(s['rootId']);item(s['rootId']).send_keys(Keys.END)
    button('Load more children').click();wait.until(lambda d:len(d.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'[role="treeitem"]'))==24)
    assert driver.execute_script('return document.activeElement.getAttribute("role")')=='treeitem'
    root=item(s['rootId']);root.send_keys(Keys.HOME,Keys.ARROW_LEFT);wait.until(lambda d:len(d.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'[role="treeitem"]'))==1)
    root.send_keys(Keys.ARROW_RIGHT);focused(s['firstChildId'])
    driver.execute_script('window.hold=arguments[0]', 'parentId='+s['rootId']);button('Load more children').click();wait.until(lambda d:d.execute_script('return Boolean(window.release)'))
    driver.execute_script('location.hash=arguments[0]','/projects/'+s['crossId']+'/issues');button('Hierarchy view').click();wait.until(lambda d:'Other project root' in d.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'[role="tree"]').text)
    driver.execute_script('window.hold=null;window.release()');assert len(driver.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'[role="treeitem"]'))==1
    assert 'Explore root' not in driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'[role="tree"]').text
    print(json.dumps({'ok':True,'checks':['root later page','root filters and complete descendants','keyboard depth and focus','child later page','collapse ownership','delayed project switch']}))
except Exception:
    if driver:print(json.dumps({'body':driver.find_element(By.TAG_NAME,'body').text,'url':driver.current_url}),file=sys.stderr)
    raise
finally:
    signal.alarm(0)
    if driver:driver.quit()
